The likelihood of `{{< meta model >}}` has no set-size variable. How strongly the target is recalled,
and in a mixture how much of the distribution goes to guessing or to non-targets, is set by the
parameters alone, whatever the number of items on the display. Set size can change the predicted
responses only through the parameters, by letting them differ between the conditions of an experiment, for example between set sizes. In
bmm that is a formula such as `{{< meta set-size-formula >}}`, in which `0 +` drops the intercept so
that every set size gets its own value of the parameter ([formula syntax](https://venpopov.com/bmm/reference/bmmformula.html)). What the model
then predicts at each set size is whatever the estimated values say, so a prediction across set sizes
needs those estimates first. No slider on this page makes a parameter depend on set size for that
reason: a curve for another set size would only be another setting of the parameters, not something
the model predicts.

The page for the [interference measurement model](imm.qmd#across-task-settings) (IMM) is the contrast.
There the distances of the other items enter the weights, so the Across set size panel on that page
moves with the parameters held fixed.
